title.narrative: Prevention Facility for the Gulf of Guinea

description.narrative: The Gulf of Guinea’s region is contending with an increasingly complex array of challenges, as evidenced by the recent surge in incidents related to violent extremism, transnational organised criminality and drug trafficking, maritime piracy, political and community violence. Local communities, especially in the northern areas bordering the Sahel, appear increasingly vulnerable to those challenges, as extremist groups and criminal organizations exploit those grievances and as their livelihoods strongly depend on the illicit markets (trafficking, smuggling, goldmining) in an area still dominated by an informal economy. These regions also face significant development challenges. Community vulnerability is accentuated by poor access to basic social infrastructure as well as proliferation of small arms and light weapons (SALW), persisting gender-based violence and climate induced conflict as well as illicit goods trafficking significantly exacerbates the risks and amplifies the intensity and reach of criminal activities. The high risk of a spillover effect from the neighbouring Sahel, where terrorist groups are expanding their activities into northern areas of Benin, Togo, Ghana, and Côte d’Ivoire which are all Neighbours to Burkina Faso which is considered as one of the epicenters for terrorist groups and violent extremisms, required a regional approach which addresses holistically the risk and bring together one Sahel country together with four costal states. The transnational nature of these threats, combined with socio-economic challenges and cross-border movements complicates efforts to prevent the spill over efforts and combat terrorist and PVE related crimes in coastal states hence the necessity of a coordinated regional response that addresses root causes and governance issues.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
